In mathematical logic, a '''Hintikka set''' is a set of [[Formula (logic)|logical formulas]] whose elements satisfy the following properties:

# An atom or its [[Negation|conjugate]] can appear in the set but not both,
# If a formula in the set has a main operator that is of "conjunctive-type", then its two operands appear in the set,
# If a formula in the set has a main operator that is of "disjunctive-type", then at least one of its two operands appears in the set.
The exact meaning of "conjunctive-type" and "disjunctive-type" is defined by the method of [[semantic tableaux]].

Hintikka sets arise when attempting to prove completeness of propositional logic using [[semantic tableaux]]. They are named after [[Jaakko Hintikka]].

== Propositional Hintikka sets ==
In a semantic tableau for [[Propositional calculus|propositional logic]], Hintikka sets can be defined using [[Method of analytic tableaux#Propositional tableau with unification|uniform notation for propositional tableaux]]. The elements of a propositional Hintikka set S satisfy the following conditions:<ref>{{Cite book |last=Smullyan |first=Raymond |title=A Beginner's Guide to Mathematical Logic |publisher=Dover |year=2014 |isbn=0486492370 |pages=91}}</ref>

# No [[Propositional variable|variable]] and its conjugate are both in S,
# For any <math>\alpha </math> in S, its components <math>\alpha_1, \alpha_2</math> are both in S,
# For any <math>\beta </math> in S, at least one of its components <math>\beta_1,\beta_2</math> are in S.
If a set S is a Hintikka set, then S is [[satisfiable]].
